blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Leading remote work is really about building explicit practices where office presence used to do the work silently. When everyone sat together, information flowed naturally. When people work remotely, that flow has to be designed — or it disappears without anyone noticing, until the team suddenly feels disconnected.

Good leaders of remote teams agree on a few simple habits. A weekly written update, short and honest. A short daily sync when it is useful, and skipped when it is not. Clear rules about response time: urgent calls are answered, while non-urgent messages are handled within 24 hours. One predictable time when everyone is available for meetings, so the rest of the day can be protected for real work.

You should set the tone yourself. If you expect your team to close their laptops at a reasonable hour, you must close yours first. Nothing a remote leader says outweighs what the team actually sees them do.

items.q: According to the text, why does information stop flowing on a remote team?
options: Because people send too many messages
Because the team is too large
Because the flow was never designed and quietly disappears
items.why: "that flow has to be designed — or it disappears without anyone noticing." No escritório o fluxo era automático.

items.q: What does the text recommend about non-urgent messages?
options: They should be discussed in the daily sync
They should be handled within 24 hours
items.why: "non-urgent messages are handled within 24 hours" — só as chamadas urgentes são atendidas na hora.

items.q: Why is there one predictable time for meetings?
options: Because remote teams cannot meet spontaneously
So the rest of the day can be protected for real work
To have more meetings each day
To replace the weekly written update
items.why: "One predictable time… so the rest of the day can be protected for real work."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A leader's example matters more than a leader's instructions.
Remote habits should be simple and agreed in advance.
Some structure has to replace what the office used to do automatically.
Sending an email about work-life balance is enough to change how a team behaves.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que "nothing a remote leader says outweighs what the team actually sees them do" — o exemplo pesa mais que o e-mail.

items.q: The sentence "you must close yours first" suggests that…
options: a leader's own behaviour sets the limit the team will follow
leaders should work fewer hours than their team
laptops should be turned off during meetings
response times should be shorter for leaders
items.why: Inferência: se o líder trabalha até tarde, a equipe copia; o tom é dado pelo exemplo, não pela regra escrita.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie falando com a equipe sobre as novas práticas remotas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, thanks for joining. I want to be honest about something before we talk about the new practices. For the last few months I have been working until midnight, and I have noticed that a lot of you started doing the same. That is on me, not on you, and it has to stop.

So here is what we are going to agree today. You should send one short written update every Friday — three lines are fine, I do not want essays. If something is genuinely urgent, you must call me; I will always pick up. But for everything else, a reply within 24 hours is perfectly acceptable. You do not have to answer messages at ten at night, and honestly, I would rather you didn't.

We will keep one fixed meeting window, right after lunch. Outside that window, you should feel free to protect your time and focus. And I have to change my own habits too — if I expect you to close your laptop at a reasonable hour, I ought to close mine first. Watch what I do, not just what I say. If I slip back into midnight emails, please push back on me.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie admit at the start?
options: She has been working until midnight and the team copied her
She wants to cancel all meetings
The written updates have been too long
items.why: "I have been working until midnight, and… a lot of you started doing the same. That is on me."

items.q: What does Sophie ask for on Fridays?
options: A video call with each person
One short written update of about three lines
A summary of every message received
items.why: "one short written update every Friday — three lines are fine, I do not want essays."

items.q: What should the team do if something is genuinely urgent?
options: Wait for the fixed meeting window
Call Sophie, because she will always pick up
items.why: "If something is genuinely urgent, you must call me; I will always pick up."

items.q: When Sophie says "That is on me, not on you," she is signalling that…
options: she takes responsibility for the overwork culture
she wants someone else to fix it
items.why: Inferência: "on me" = a responsabilidade é dela; ela assume ter dado o mau exemplo.

items.q: Why does Sophie ask the team to "push back" on her if she slips?
options: Because she wants to reduce the number of meetings
Because she does not trust her own judgement
Because she knows her example matters more than her words
Because the team decides her working hours
items.why: Inferência: ela pede que a corrijam justamente porque o tom é dado pelo comportamento dela, não pelo discurso.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "On a remote team you need an explicit practice, not a vague expectation." An explicit practice is…
options: a habit that is clearly stated and agreed
items.why: Explicit practice = prática explícita: um hábito claro e combinado, não algo implícito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Without a shared meeting slot, information stops flowing and the team starts to feel ___."
items.why: Disconnected = desconectado: é o que acontece quando o fluxo de informação some.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We agreed a clear ___: urgent calls are answered at once, other messages within 24 hours."
items.why: Response time = tempo de resposta, exatamente a regra descrita na frase.

items.q: "In the office, coordination happened through office presence alone." This phrase refers to…
options: the number of desks in the room
people being physically together, so information spread by itself
items.why: Office presence = presença física; era o que fazia a informação circular sozinha.

items.q: "A good leader has to set the tone for the whole team." To set the tone means to…
options: establish the mood and standard others will follow
items.why: Set the tone = dar o tom: definir, pelo exemplo, o padrão que a equipe vai seguir.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre trabalho remoto e gestão de equipes. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the new remote policy team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, área por área.

items.q: "The team agreed the new habits but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "If Sophie starts sending midnight emails again, we should push back on it." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "HR still has to sign off on the new response-time rules." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Protecting the afternoon for focused work really did move the needle on output." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.
